aws-soa-c03-s4.2-07.title: Promote a replica secret to a standalone secret in AWS Secrets Manager

aws-soa-c03-s1.2-06.reason: explanation_error: the explanation presented the resource-based policy as the only route. The page now documents an IAM execution role on the target as an alternative. Statement kept. (final: keep)
aws-soa-c03-s1.2-06.statement: A Lambda function's resource-based policy can grant EventBridge permission to invoke the function.
aws-soa-c03-s1.2-06.explanation: A resource-based policy that grants lambda:InvokeFunction to events.amazonaws.com authorizes the rule. EventBridge relies on it when no IAM execution role is configured on the target.

source.title: Using resource-based policies for Amazon EventBridge

aws-soa-c03-s1.3-06.reason: weak_card (giveaway 'On first access ... moves accessed files back'). Rewritten rather than dropped, because dropping 03, 06 and 09 would leave 1.3 at 3 true out of 9. It now tests the default behaviour. Page: 'By default, files are not moved back to the Standard storage class, and they remain in the IA or Archive storage class when they are accessed.' (final: keep)
aws-soa-c03-s1.3-06.statement: By default, Amazon EFS leaves a file in the IA storage class when an application reads its content.
aws-soa-c03-s1.3-06.explanation: The Transition into Standard lifecycle policy leaves accessed files in IA or Archive by default. Setting it to On first access moves them back to Standard for latency-sensitive workloads.

aws-soa-c03-s2.2-03.reason: weak_card (HealthThreshold name giveaway). Rewritten rather than dropped, because dropping 03, 07 and 11 would leave 2.2 at 3 true out of 9. Page: 'If you disable a health check that a calculated health check is monitoring, Route 53 considers the disabled health check to be healthy ... choose the Invert health check status check box.' (final: keep)
aws-soa-c03-s2.2-03.statement: Amazon Route 53 treats a disabled child health check as healthy while it evaluates the parent calculated health check.
aws-soa-c03-s2.2-03.explanation: A disabled health check that a calculated health check monitors is treated as healthy. To have Route 53 count it as unhealthy instead, an operator inverts its health check status.

source.title: Values that you specify when you create or update health checks

aws-soa-c03-s2.3-10.reason: weak_card (definition card, near-copy of the source). Rewritten rather than dropped, because dropping 01, 10 and 11 would leave 2.3 at 3 true out of 9. Page: 'All shadow copies stored in your file system are included in file system backups.' and 'Shadow copies are not enabled on FSx for Windows File Server by default.' (final: keep)
aws-soa-c03-s2.3-10.statement: Backups of an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system include the shadow copies stored on it.
aws-soa-c03-s2.3-10.explanation: Shadow copies are stored alongside the file system's data, so file system backups capture them. Shadow copies are off by default; an operator enables and schedules them with PowerShell commands.

source.title: Protecting your data with shadow copies

aws-soa-c03-s2.3-12.reason: ambiguous: the 'using Amazon EC2 ... reduced capacity' framing matches the whitepaper's own pilot light subsection ('EC2 instances are deployed in a scaled-down configuration'). The new statement names neither EC2 nor capacity, does not reveal that the servers are off, and rests on the Note: 'pilot light cannot process requests without additional action taken first ... requires you to turn on servers'. (final: fixed)
aws-soa-c03-s2.3-12.statement: In the AWS pilot light strategy, the recovery Region handles requests the moment failover begins.
aws-soa-c03-s2.3-12.explanation: Pilot light keeps data stores live but application servers switched off, so the recovery Region cannot process requests until they are turned on. Warm standby serves traffic at reduced capacity immediately.
aws-soa-c03-s2.3-12.misconception: A pilot light recovery Region already runs application servers that take traffic the moment it is redirected.

source.title: Disaster recovery options in the cloud

aws-soa-c03-s4.2-06.reason: ambiguous: 'keeps clone permissions' can be read as 'keeps them in sync', and it named the template as the actor. Page: 'Secrets Manager creates the cloned user with the same permissions as the original user. If you change the original user's permissions after the clone is created, you must also change the cloned user's permissions.' (final: keep)
aws-soa-c03-s4.2-06.statement: With alternating users rotation, an operator who changes the original user's permissions must also update the clone.
aws-soa-c03-s4.2-06.explanation: Secrets Manager creates the clone with the original user's permissions during the first rotation. Later permission changes to the original user do not carry over to the clone.

aws-soa-c03-s4.2-07.reason: source_problem: replicate-secrets.html never says a replica cannot rotate on its own. standalone-secret.html says 'A replica secret can't be updated independently from its primary secret, except for its encryption key' and suggests promoting a replica 'if you want to turn on rotation for the replica'. Statement kept; explanation aligned with the new page. (final: keep)
aws-soa-c03-s4.2-07.statement: AWS Secrets Manager can rotate a replica secret independently while its replication link remains active.
aws-soa-c03-s4.2-07.explanation: A replica secret can't be updated independently of its primary, apart from its KMS key. To turn on rotation for a replica, an operator promotes it to a standalone secret.
aws-soa-c03-s4.2-07.misconception: An active replica secret has a rotation schedule independent of its primary secret.

source.title: Promote a replica secret to a standalone secret in AWS Secrets Manager

aws-soa-c03-s3.1-07.reason: source_problem (the verifier's optional improvement): the API reference only implies the fact. The user guide page states it: 'A stack in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state can't be updated, but it can be rolled back to a working state (UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE).' Text unchanged. (final: keep)
aws-soa-c03-s3.1-07.statement: AWS CloudFormation can accept a new stack update while the stack is in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED.
aws-soa-c03-s3.1-07.explanation: A stack in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED needs recovery before another update. The operator can use ContinueUpdateRollback to restore it to UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE.
aws-soa-c03-s3.1-07.misconception: A new stack update can repair UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED before rollback recovery.

aws-soa-c03-s2.3-06.statement: Apart from the first, each Amazon EBS snapshot of a volume saves only blocks changed or added since the last snapshot.
aws-soa-c03-s2.3-06.explanation: The first snapshot of a volume is a full snapshot. Later incremental snapshots save only new and changed blocks and reference unchanged data stored in earlier snapshots.

aws-soa-c03-s2.2-04.statement: Amazon Route 53 health checkers probe an endpoint's private IP address inside an Amazon VPC.
aws-soa-c03-s2.2-04.explanation: Route 53 health checkers run outside the VPC, so an endpoint checked by IP address needs a public IP. For instances with only private IPs, a health check can monitor a CloudWatch alarm instead.
aws-soa-c03-s2.2-04.misconception: Route 53 endpoint health checkers reach private VPC addresses directly.

aws-soa-c03-s1.1-02.statement: A CloudWatch composite alarm can evaluate a rule expression built from raw metric values.
aws-soa-c03-s1.1-02.explanation: A composite alarm applies a logical rule to the states of other alarms. Its inputs are alarm states such as ALARM, OK, and INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
aws-soa-c03-s1.1-02.misconception: Composite alarms aggregate metric values rather than evaluate other alarms' states.

aws-soa-c03-s1.1-05.explanation: CloudWatch dashboards bring metrics from different Regions into one view. Widget or metric settings identify the Region supplying the data.

aws-soa-c03-s3.2-09.statement: Amazon S3 Event Notifications preserve the order of the object operations that generated them.
aws-soa-c03-s3.2-09.explanation: Amazon S3 Event Notifications are delivered at least once and aren't guaranteed to arrive in the same order as the object operations that generated them.
